18512.q: At what time does the Morgestraich begin at the Basel carnival?
18512.e: On the Monday after Ash Wednesday, all the lights go out at 4 o'clock in the morning. Then drummers and piccolo players march through the city.
18512.m: The Morgestraich begins at four in the morning.

18513.q: What can you see on the coat of arms of Basel-Stadt?
18513.e: The coat of arms of Basel-Stadt shows a black Basel crosier on a white background. It looks like a bishop's staff.
18513.m: The Basel crosier is the symbol of Basel.

18514.q: What do the people of Basel affectionately call their zoo?
18514.e: Basel Zoo is the oldest zoo in Switzerland. In Basel people simply call it “Zolli”.
18514.m: Basel Zoo is called the Zolli.

18515.q: What are the well-known spiced biscuits from Basel called?
18515.e: Basler Läckerli are small, hard gingerbread biscuits with honey and spices. They are known all over Switzerland.
18515.m: Läckerli are gingerbread biscuits from Basel.

18516.q: What is the famous fountain in the harbour of Geneva called?
18516.e: The Jet d'eau shoots water about 140 metres into the air. It is the landmark of Geneva.
18516.m: The Jet d'eau is the landmark of Geneva.

18517.q: Which language do most people in Geneva speak?
18517.e: Geneva is in French-speaking Switzerland. People there mainly speak French.

18518.q: Which big organisation has an important office in Geneva?
18518.e: The United Nations, the UN for short, has its European headquarters in Geneva. People from all over the world meet there.
18518.m: The UN has an office in Geneva.

18519.q: What can you admire in the English Garden in Geneva?
18519.e: The Flower Clock stands in the English Garden. Its face is made of thousands of flowers.
18519.m: Geneva has a clock made of flowers.

18520.q: Which festival is celebrated in Geneva in December with pots made of chocolate?
18520.e: At the Escalade, Geneva remembers an attack in 1602 that was fought off. Children smash a pot made of chocolate.
18520.m: At the Escalade you smash a chocolate pot.

18521.q: What is the famous old wooden bridge in Lucerne called?
18521.e: The Chapel Bridge is a covered wooden bridge over the Reuss. Old paintings hang under its roof.
18521.m: The Chapel Bridge is the landmark of Lucerne.

18522.q: Which animal is shown on the famous monument in the rock in Lucerne?
18522.e: The Lion Monument shows a dying lion carved into the rock. It remembers Swiss soldiers who died in Paris in 1792.
18522.m: There is a stone lion in Lucerne.

18523.q: What is the tower that stands in the water next to the Chapel Bridge called?
18523.e: The Water Tower stands in the river next to the Chapel Bridge. It is octagonal and very old.
18523.m: The Water Tower stands next to the Chapel Bridge.

18524.q: Which mountain is right next to Lucerne?
18524.e: Pilatus is Lucerne's local mountain. The steepest cogwheel railway in the world goes up it.

18525.q: Which animal with large curved horns lives in the Alps?
18525.e: The ibex climbs very skilfully on steep rocks. The males have long, curved horns.
18525.m: The ibex climbs in the Alps.

18526.q: Which Alpine animal whistles loudly when there is danger?
18526.e: Marmots warn each other with a loud whistle. Then they all quickly disappear into their burrow.
18526.m: The marmot whistles when there is danger.

18527.q: Which well-known Alpine flower has white, woolly flowers?
18527.e: Edelweiss grows high up in the mountains. Its flowers are covered with fine white hairs.

18528.q: What do you call a large mass of ice that slowly flows down the valley in the mountains?
18528.e: A glacier forms from snow that turns into ice over many years. The largest glacier in the Alps is the Great Aletsch Glacier.
18528.m: A glacier is a river of ice.

18529.q: In which canton is the Matterhorn?
18529.e: The Matterhorn is in the canton of Valais. It is one of the best-known mountains in the world.

18530.q: Which village lies at the foot of the Matterhorn?
18530.e: Zermatt lies right below the Matterhorn. No ordinary petrol cars drive in the village.
18530.m: Zermatt lies at the foot of the Matterhorn.

18531.q: Roughly how high is the Matterhorn?
18531.e: The Matterhorn is 4,478 metres high. That is about 4,500 metres.
18531.m: The Matterhorn is almost 4,500 metres high.

18532.q: Which neighbouring country does Switzerland share the Matterhorn with?
18532.e: The border with Italy runs over the summit of the Matterhorn. In Italian the mountain is called Monte Cervino.
18532.m: The Matterhorn is on the border with Italy.

18533.e: The Matterhorn has four steep sides and a point. That is why it looks like a pyramid.
18533.m: The Matterhorn looks like a pyramid.

18534.q: What is the famous waterfall near Schaffhausen called?
18534.e: The Rhine Falls near Schaffhausen are one of the most powerful waterfalls in Europe. They are 23 metres high and 150 metres wide.
18534.m: The Rhine Falls are near Schaffhausen.

18535.q: Roughly how long is the Rhine?
18535.e: The Rhine is about 1,230 kilometres long. It is one of the longest rivers in Europe.
18535.m: The Rhine is about 1,200 kilometres long.

18536.q: Which river forms part of the border between Switzerland and Germany?
18536.e: Between Schaffhausen and Basel the Rhine often flows exactly along the border. Switzerland is on one side and Germany on the other.
18536.m: The Rhine is a border river with Germany.

18537.q: Which is the longest river that flows entirely within Switzerland?
18537.e: The Aare is almost 300 kilometres long. From its source to its mouth it flows only through Switzerland.
18537.m: The Aare is the longest river entirely in Switzerland.

18538.q: In which canton does the Aare rise?
18538.e: The Aare rises from glaciers in the Bernese Alps. That is near the Grimsel Pass.
18538.m: The Aare rises in the canton of Bern.

18539.q: Which river does the Aare flow into?
18539.e: At Koblenz in the canton of Aargau, the Aare flows into a bigger river. There it often carries more water than that river.
18539.m: The Aare flows into the Rhine.

18540.q: Which two lakes does the Aare flow through in the Bernese Oberland?
18540.e: The Aare first flows through Lake Brienz and then through Lake Thun. Interlaken lies between the lakes.
18540.m: The Aare flows through Lake Brienz and Lake Thun.

18541.q: Which town in the canton of Aargau gets its name from the Aare?
18541.e: Aarau lies on the Aare and is the capital of the canton of Aargau. The name Aargau also comes from the river.
18541.m: Aarau gets its name from the Aare.

18542.q: Which is the largest lake that Switzerland has a share in?
18542.e: Lake Geneva covers about 580 square kilometres. It has the shape of a crescent moon.
18542.m: Lake Geneva is the largest lake on which Switzerland lies.

18543.q: What is Lake Geneva called in French?
18543.e: In French-speaking Switzerland, Lake Geneva is called “Lac Léman”. The name is very old.
18543.m: In French, Lake Geneva is called Lac Léman.

18544.q: Which country does Switzerland share Lake Geneva with?
18544.e: The north shore belongs to Switzerland, and a large part of the south shore to France. The border runs through the middle of the lake.
18544.m: Lake Geneva is also in France.

18545.q: Which river flows into Lake Geneva and out again?
18545.e: The Rhône comes from Valais into Lake Geneva. At the other end it flows on into France.
18545.m: The Rhône flows through Lake Geneva.

18546.q: Which castle stands right on the shore of Lake Geneva near Montreux?
18546.e: Chillon Castle stands on a rock in the water. It is one of the best-known castles in Switzerland.
18546.m: Chillon Castle stands on Lake Geneva.

18547.q: Which three countries border Lake Constance?
18547.e: Three countries meet at Lake Constance. Their shores all lie on the same lake.
18547.m: Three countries lie on Lake Constance.

18548.q: Which flower island is in Lake Constance?
18548.e: The island of Mainau is known for its many flowers and gardens. It belongs to Germany.
18548.m: Mainau is the flower island in Lake Constance.

18549.q: Which Swiss canton lies on Lake Constance?
18549.e: Thurgau has a long shore on Lake Constance. Places like Romanshorn and Kreuzlingen are there.

18550.q: Which big river flows into Lake Constance?
18550.e: The Rhine flows into Lake Constance in Austria, not far from Bregenz. It flows out again at Stein am Rhein.
18550.m: The Rhine flows through Lake Constance.

18551.q: What is the Bodensee called in English?
18551.e: In English the Bodensee is called “Lake Constance”. The name comes from the town of Konstanz on the lake.
18551.m: In English the Bodensee is called Lake Constance.

18552.q: How many centimes make one franc?
18552.e: One franc has 100 centimes. So two 50-centime coins together make one franc.

18553.q: Which is the largest Swiss banknote?
18553.e: The largest banknote in Switzerland is worth 1,000 francs (as of 2025). It is purple.
18553.m: The largest banknote is the 1,000-franc note.

18554.e: Every Swiss banknote has its own colour. The 50-franc note is green.

18555.q: You have 2 francs and 50 centimes. How many centimes is that?
18555.m: Two francs and fifty centimes are 250 centimes.

18556.q: Which national language do the most people in Switzerland speak?
18556.e: About 6 out of 10 people in Switzerland mainly speak German. In everyday life they mostly speak Swiss German.
18556.m: German is the most common language in Switzerland.

18557.q: Which national language is spoken almost only in the canton of the Grisons?
18557.e: Romansh is spoken almost only in the canton of the Grisons. It is the smallest national language.
18557.m: Romansh is spoken in the Grisons.

18558.q: What does the Italian word “Grazie” mean in English?
18558.e: You say “Grazie” to thank someone in Italian. In French you say “Merci”.

18559.q: What is the very long wooden musical instrument that is blown in the mountains called?
18559.e: The alphorn is often more than three metres long. In the past people used it to call across long distances in the mountains.
18559.m: The alphorn is a Swiss instrument.

18560.q: What is the Swiss sport called in which two men or women wrestle in sawdust?
18560.e: In Schwingen two people grab each other by short fabric trousers. Whoever puts the other on their back wins.
18560.m: In Schwingen people wrestle in sawdust.

18561.q: Which cheese dish is eaten together from one pot?
18561.e: For fondue, cheese melts in a pot. Everyone dips bread into it on long forks.
18561.m: Fondue is eaten together from one pot.

18562.q: Who visits children in Switzerland on 6 December?
18562.e: On 6 December Samichlaus, the Swiss Saint Nicholas, comes. He brings nuts, mandarins and gingerbread.

18563.q: What happens at the Alpabzug in autumn?
a: The cows come down from the alpine pasture to the valley
People ski down to the valley
People plant trees on the alpine pasture
People build huts on the alpine pasture
18563.e: In summer the cows are up on the alpine pasture. In autumn they are brought down to the valley, decorated with flowers and bells.
18563.m: At the Alpabzug the cows come down to the valley.

18564.q: What do people often light on hills and mountains on the evening of National Day?
18564.e: In the evening big fires burn on many hills. They are called bonfires on the heights.

18565.q: What do children often carry through the streets on the evening of 1 August?
18565.e: Lampions are colourful paper lanterns. They are often painted with Swiss crosses.

18566.e: In the Federal Charter of 1291 three valley communities promised to help each other. This is seen as the beginning of the Swiss Confederation.

18567.q: The Rütli meadow is an important place for 1 August. Which lake is it on?
18567.e: The Rütli meadow is in the canton of Uri, high above Lake Lucerne. Many people visit it on National Day.
18567.m: The Rütli is on Lake Lucerne.

18568.q: Which town is the capital of the canton of Ticino?
18568.e: Lugano is the largest town in Ticino, but the capital is Bellinzona with its three castles.
18568.m: The capital of Ticino is Bellinzona, not Lugano.

18569.q: Which town is the capital of the canton of Valais?
18569.e: The capital of Valais is called Sion in French and Sitten in German.
18569.m: Sion, Sitten in German, is the capital of Valais.

18570.q: Which town is the capital of the canton of Jura?
18570.e: The youngest canton in Switzerland has Delémont as its capital.
18570.m: Delémont is the capital of the canton of Jura.

18571.q: Where are the government and parliament of the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden based?
18571.e: Herisau is the seat of the government and cantonal parliament of Appenzell Ausserrhoden. Appenzell is the capital of the neighbouring canton of Innerrhoden.
18571.m: Herisau is the seat of government of Appenzell Ausserrhoden.

18572.q: Which place is the capital of the canton of Nidwalden?
18572.e: Stans is the capital of Nidwalden, and Sarnen that of Obwalden.
18572.m: Stans is the capital of the canton of Nidwalden.

18573.q: Which region lies between the Jura and the Alps and is the most densely populated?
18573.e: On the Swiss Plateau, between Lake Geneva and Lake Constance, are most of the big cities, and most people live there.
18573.m: Most people in Switzerland live on the Swiss Plateau.

18574.q: Roughly how much of Switzerland's area belongs to the Alps?
18574.e: The Alps and Pre-Alps together cover about three fifths of Switzerland, the Swiss Plateau almost a third and the Jura about a tenth.
18574.m: About three fifths of Switzerland lies in the Alps.

18575.q: What is the French-speaking part of Switzerland called?
18575.e: French-speaking western Switzerland is called Romandie.
18575.m: The French-speaking west of Switzerland is called Romandie.

18576.q: In which canton is Romansh used as an official language?
18576.e: The Grisons has three languages: German, Italian and Romansh.
18576.m: Romansh is an official language in the canton of the Grisons.

18577.q: In which canton is Italian the only official language?
18577.e: Ticino is the only canton where Italian is the only official language.
18577.m: In Ticino, Italian is the only official language.

18578.q: What is the region with the cantons of Lucerne, Uri, Schwyz, Obwalden, Nidwalden and Zug called?
18578.e: Central Switzerland lies around Lake Lucerne. The founding cantons of the Confederation are also here.
18578.m: Lucerne, Uri and Schwyz belong to Central Switzerland.

18579.q: With which neighbouring country does Switzerland have the longest border?
18579.e: At more than 700 kilometres, the border with Italy is Switzerland's longest national border.
18579.m: Switzerland's longest border is the one with Italy.

18580.q: With which neighbouring country does Switzerland have the shortest border?
18580.e: The border with Liechtenstein is only about 41 kilometres long and mostly follows the Rhine.
18580.m: Switzerland's shortest national border is the one with Liechtenstein.

18581.q: Which currency do people pay with in Liechtenstein?
18581.e: Liechtenstein has no currency of its own and has used the Swiss franc since 1924.
18581.m: In Liechtenstein people also pay with Swiss francs.

18582.q: Which neighbouring country does the canton of Geneva border?
18582.e: The canton of Geneva is almost completely surrounded by France and is linked to Vaud only by a narrow strip.
18582.m: The canton of Geneva is almost entirely surrounded by France.

18583.q: Which mountain massif does the highest peak in Switzerland belong to?
18583.e: The highest Swiss peak is the main summit of the Monte Rosa massif in Valais.
18583.m: The highest peak in Switzerland belongs to the Monte Rosa massif.

18584.q: Which mountain range lies in the north-west of Switzerland along the border with France?
18584.e: The Jura is a limestone mountain range that stretches from Geneva to Schaffhausen.
18584.m: The Jura lies in the north-west of Switzerland.

18585.q: Which Alpine pass links the canton of Uri with Ticino?
18585.e: The Gotthard Pass leads from Andermatt in the canton of Uri to Airolo in Ticino.
18585.m: The Gotthard Pass links Uri with Ticino.

18586.q: Which is the longest river that runs entirely within Switzerland?
18586.e: The Aare is 288 kilometres long and flows from the Bernese Alps to where it joins the Rhine at Koblenz in Aargau.
18586.m: The Aare is the longest river that flows entirely within Switzerland.

18587.q: Which river from the Engadine carries its water via the Danube to the Black Sea?
18587.e: The Inn rises in the Engadine, flows through Austria and joins the Danube at Passau.
18587.m: The Inn carries water from the Engadine all the way to the Black Sea.

18588.q: Which sea does the water of the Ticino reach?
18588.e: The Ticino flows through Lake Maggiore into the Po, which flows into the Adriatic.
18588.m: The Ticino drains via the Po into the Adriatic.

18590.q: Which is the largest lake that lies entirely within Switzerland?
18590.e: Lake Neuchâtel covers about 215 square kilometres and lies entirely on Swiss soil.
18590.m: Lake Neuchâtel is the largest lake entirely in Switzerland.

18591.q: Which is the largest lake that Switzerland has a share in?
18591.e: Lake Geneva covers about 580 square kilometres. Almost 60 per cent of it belongs to Switzerland, and the rest, with most of the south shore, to France.
18591.m: Lake Geneva is the largest lake with a Swiss share.

18592.q: Apart from Switzerland, which countries lie on Lake Constance?
18592.e: Switzerland, Germany and Austria meet at Lake Constance.
18592.m: Three countries border each other at Lake Constance.

18593.q: Which lake lies partly in Switzerland and partly in Italy?
18593.e: The northern part of Lake Maggiore, with Locarno, belongs to Switzerland, and the larger part to Italy.
18593.m: Lake Maggiore lies in Switzerland and Italy.

18594.q: Which town lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz?
18594.e: The name Interlaken means “between the lakes”.
18594.m: Interlaken lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.

18595.q: For how many years is the Federal Council elected?
18595.e: The Federal Council is elected for a four-year term after each general election of the National Council.
18595.m: The Federal Council's term of office is four years.

18596.q: How long does the office of President of the Swiss Confederation last?
18596.e: Each year one member of the Federal Council becomes President of the Confederation and chairs the meetings.
18596.m: The presidency of the Confederation changes every year.

18597.q: What is the sharing of Federal Council seats that applied from 1959 to 2003 called?
18597.e: The magic formula shared the seven seats among the four largest parties in the ratio 2 to 2 to 2 to 1.
18597.m: The magic formula shared the Federal Council seats among the large parties.

18598.q: What does the number of National Council seats a canton has depend on?
a: on the age of the canton
18598.e: The 200 seats are shared among the cantons according to their population.
18598.m: Large cantons have more seats in the National Council than small ones.

18599.q: What is the minimum number of National Council seats each canton has?
18599.e: The Federal Constitution guarantees every canton at least one seat in the National Council, even if it has few inhabitants.
18599.m: Every canton has at least one seat in the National Council.

18600.q: Which canton has the most members of the National Council?
18600.e: As the canton with the largest population, Zurich has had 36 seats since the 2023 elections.
18600.m: Zurich has the most seats in the National Council.

18601.q: In which building does the National Council meet?
a: in the Federal Palace in Bern
in the Town Hall in Zurich
in the Palais des Nations in Geneva
in the Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne
18601.e: The National Council and the Council of States meet in the parliament building of the Federal Palace in Bern.
18601.m: Parliament meets in the Federal Palace in Bern.

18602.q: How many ordinary sessions does parliament hold each year?
18602.e: There are the spring, summer, autumn and winter sessions, which usually last three weeks each.
18602.m: Parliament meets for four ordinary sessions every year.

18603.q: How many members of the Council of States does the canton of Basel-Stadt have?
18603.e: The former half-cantons, such as Basel-Stadt and Basel-Landschaft, each have one member in the Council of States.
18603.m: Basel-Stadt has one seat in the Council of States.

18604.q: Who decides how the members of the Council of States are elected?
18604.e: Elections to the Council of States are regulated by each canton. Most cantons use a majority voting system.
18604.m: Each canton decides for itself how its members of the Council of States are elected.

18605.q: What else is the Council of States called?
18605.e: With 46 members, the Council of States is the smaller of the two chambers of parliament and represents the cantons.
18605.m: The Council of States is the small chamber and represents the cantons.

18606.q: What is needed for parliament to pass a new federal law?
a: The Council of States decides alone.
18606.e: The National Council and the Council of States have equal rights. A law is only passed if both chambers agree on the same text.
18606.m: A federal law needs the approval of the National Council and the Council of States.

18607.q: Since which year have women in Switzerland been allowed to vote and stand for election at federal level?
18607.e: On 7 February 1971 the men voted in favour of women's right to vote and stand for election at federal level.
18607.m: Since 1971 women have had the right to vote at federal level.

18608.q: Which canton was the last to introduce women's right to vote at cantonal level?
18608.e: In 1990 the Federal Supreme Court forced Appenzell Innerrhoden to give women the right to vote in the canton.
18608.m: Appenzell Innerrhoden was the last canton to introduce women's right to vote, in 1990.

18609.q: On which three political levels is Switzerland built?
18609.e: In Swiss federalism, the Confederation, the cantons and the municipalities each have their own tasks.
18609.m: Switzerland is made up of the Confederation, the cantons and the municipalities.

18610.q: What does a popular initiative need in order to be approved?
a: A majority of the people and of the cantons
Only a majority of the people
Only a majority of the cantons
The approval of the Federal Council
18610.e: Because a popular initiative changes the constitution, both the majority of voters and the majority of the cantons must agree.
18610.m: A popular initiative needs a yes from the people and the cantons.

18611.q: What must the people always vote on?
a: on changes to the Federal Constitution
on the election of the Federal Council
18611.e: Changes to the constitution are subject to a mandatory referendum. People only vote on laws if a referendum is called.
18611.m: Every change to the Federal Constitution is put to the people.

18612.q: On how many dates per year are federal votes usually held?
18612.e: The Federal Council usually sets four voting Sundays each year.
18612.m: There are usually four federal voting Sundays each year.

18613.q: Which canton was the first to introduce a voting age of 16 in 2007?
18613.e: In 2007 the Landsgemeinde in Glarus decided that young people from the age of 16 may have a say in the canton.
18613.m: In 2007 Glarus became the first canton with a voting age of 16.

18614.q: How many cantonal votes are there in total in a vote?
18614.e: Twenty cantons have a full cantonal vote and six cantons have half a vote. 20 plus 6 times 0.5 makes 23.
18614.m: There are 23 cantonal votes in total.

18615.q: In which year will the next general election of the National Council take place (as of 2026)?
18615.e: The National Council is elected every four years. After the 2023 election, the next one follows in autumn 2027.
18615.m: The National Council is elected every four years.

18616.q: Which system is used to elect the National Council in most cantons?
18616.e: With proportional representation, parties get seats in proportion to their votes. Only cantons with one seat use majority voting.
18616.m: The National Council is mostly elected by proportional representation.

18617.q: What is it called when you write names of candidates from other lists onto an election list?
18617.e: With panachage you mix candidates from different parties on one list.
18617.m: Mixing names from different lists is called panachage.

18618.q: Which party won the largest share of the vote in the 2023 National Council elections?
18618.e: In 2023 the SVP won about 28 per cent of the vote and remained the party with the most voters.
18618.m: The SVP was the strongest party in 2023.

18619.q: In which year did Switzerland get its first Federal Constitution?
18619.e: With the Federal Constitution of 1848, Switzerland changed from a confederation of states into a federal state.
18619.m: Switzerland has been a federal state since 1848.

18620.q: Since when has today's Federal Constitution been in force?
18620.e: The people and the cantons approved the new constitution in 1999. It came into force on 1 January 2000.
18620.m: Today's Federal Constitution has been in force since 2000.

18621.q: What is the most important law in Switzerland, which also contains the fundamental rights, called?
18621.e: The Federal Constitution stands above all other laws. It sets out the fundamental rights and how the state is organised.
18621.m: The Federal Constitution is the most important law in Switzerland.

18622.q: How many national languages does the Federal Constitution name?
18622.e: Article 4 names German, French, Italian and Romansh as national languages.

18623.q: What is Bern officially called as the seat of the Federal Council and parliament?
18623.e: Officially, Switzerland has no capital. Bern is the federal city.
18623.m: Bern is officially the federal city of Switzerland.

18624.q: At which congress was Switzerland's neutrality recognised by the great powers in 1815?
18624.e: At the Congress of Vienna after the Napoleonic Wars, the European powers recognised Switzerland's permanent neutrality.
18624.m: Switzerland's neutrality was recognised at the Congress of Vienna in 1815.

18625.q: Which organisation is neutral Switzerland NOT a member of?
18625.e: As a neutral state, Switzerland does not belong to any military alliance.
18625.m: Neutral Switzerland does not belong to any military alliance.

18626.q: What are neutral Switzerland's mediation work and protecting power mandates called?
18626.e: Through its good offices, Switzerland mediates between states or represents countries that have no relations with each other.
18626.m: Through its good offices, Switzerland helps to mediate in conflicts.

18627.q: After which defeat in 1515 did the Confederation withdraw from the wars of the great powers?
18627.e: After the defeat at Marignano in northern Italy, the Confederates gave up playing power politics. This is seen as the beginning of neutrality.
18627.m: After Marignano in 1515, Switzerland began to stay out of foreign wars.

18628.q: Which three communities made the Federal Charter in 1291?
18628.e: The Federal Charter of early August 1291 is seen as the founding document of the Confederation.
18628.m: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden made the Federal Charter in 1291.

18629.q: In which year did the Battle of Morgarten take place?
18629.e: At Morgarten in 1315, the men of Schwyz defeated a Habsburg army.
18629.m: The Battle of Morgarten was in 1315.

18630.q: According to legend, which hero sacrificed himself in the Battle of Sempach in 1386?
18630.e: According to legend, Winkelried grabbed the enemy's lances and so opened a gap for the Confederates.
18630.m: Arnold Winkelried is the legendary hero of the Battle of Sempach.

18631.q: What was the unitary state that the French set up in Switzerland in 1798 called?
18631.e: After the French invasion, the Helvetic Republic replaced the Old Swiss Confederacy from 1798 to 1803.
18631.m: The Helvetic Republic was created in 1798 under French influence.

18632.q: What is Switzerland's last civil war of 1847 called?
18632.e: In the Sonderbund War the liberal cantons defeated seven Catholic conservative cantons.
18632.m: The Sonderbund War of 1847 was Switzerland's last civil war.

18633.q: According to legend, in which place did William Tell shoot the apple off his son's head?
18633.e: On the village square of Altdorf in the canton of Uri, a monument recalls the apple shot.
18633.m: William Tell's apple shot took place in Altdorf.

18634.q: Which man from Geneva founded the Red Cross and received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901?
18634.e: Henry Dunant witnessed the Battle of Solferino in 1859 and then proposed founding the Red Cross.
18634.m: Henry Dunant is the founder of the Red Cross.

18635.q: Which writer wrote the stories about “Heidi”?
18635.e: Johanna Spyri from Hirzel published the Heidi books in 1880 and 1881.
18635.m: Johanna Spyri is the author of “Heidi”.

18636.q: Which physicist developed the special theory of relativity in Bern in 1905?
18636.e: Einstein was working at the patent office in Bern at the time and published several groundbreaking papers in 1905.
18636.m: Albert Einstein developed the theory of relativity in Bern.

18637.q: Which world-famous architect comes from La Chaux-de-Fonds?
18637.e: Le Corbusier's real name was Charles-Édouard Jeanneret. Several of his buildings are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
18637.m: Le Corbusier was born in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

18638.q: How many Grand Slam singles titles did Roger Federer win?
18638.e: Between 2003 and 2018 Federer won twenty Grand Slam singles tournaments, eight of them at Wimbledon.
18638.m: Roger Federer won 20 Grand Slam titles.

18639.q: Which educator from Zurich wanted children to learn with “head, heart and hand”?
18639.e: Around 1800 Pestalozzi worked for the education of poor children and shaped state schooling.
18639.m: Pestalozzi wanted children to learn with head, heart and hand.

18640.q: In which town does the food company Nestlé have its headquarters?
18640.e: Nestlé has its headquarters in Vevey on Lake Geneva.

18641.e: Gottlieb Duttweiler first sold goods from lorries. Later he turned Migros into cooperatives.

18642.q: What does the abbreviation SBB stand for?
18642.e: Swiss Federal Railways was formed in 1902 from several private railway companies.
18642.m: SBB stands for Swiss Federal Railways.

18643.q: In which city do the pharmaceutical companies Roche and Novartis have their headquarters?
18643.e: Basel is the centre of the Swiss pharmaceutical and chemical industry.

18644.q: Which industry is especially important in the Jura arc from Geneva to Schaffhausen?
18644.e: Places such as La Chaux-de-Fonds, Le Locle and Biel are known worldwide for making watches.
18644.m: Many Swiss watches are made in the Jura arc.

18645.q: What did an engineer from French-speaking Switzerland invent after finding burrs in his dog's fur?
18645.e: George de Mestral saw how the tiny hooks of the burrs held on to the fur. Using this as a model, he made the hook-and-loop fastener, known as Velcro, and patented it in 1951.
18645.m: The hook-and-loop fastener was invented in Switzerland.

18646.q: Which kitchen tool from Switzerland is called “Rex”?
18646.e: The “Rex” peeler was invented in Switzerland in 1947. With its moving blade you can peel potatoes and carrots thinly.
18646.m: The “Rex” peeler is a Swiss invention.

18647.q: Which sweet was invented in 1875 in Vevey on Lake Geneva?
18647.e: Daniel Peter was the first to mix condensed milk into chocolate. This created milk chocolate, for which Switzerland is famous.
18647.m: Milk chocolate was invented in Switzerland.

18648.q: What is the see-through film called that a Swiss chemist invented in 1908?
18648.e: Jacques Brandenberger wanted to make a tablecloth that stains would not stick to. In doing so he invented the see-through film cellophane.
